query: High-entropy alloys contain five or more elements at 5–35 at% each, generally with comparable atomic radii. Refractory and nickel-based high-entropy alloys have demonstrated elevated-temperature mechanical properties comparable to titanium- and nickel-based alloys used in extreme environments because of their heat resistance and specific strength. However, prior investigations have mainly treated titanium and nickel as additions, leaving alloys in which both are primary constituents unexplored. Subject to the stated compositional definition, what single testable intervention hypothesis could improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy relative to the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted relative outcome, composition and operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled post-casting aging treatment that induces nano-scale precipitate formation will improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium‐ and nickel‐primary high-entropy alloy compared to its as-cast single-phase form.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-cast, single-phase high-entropy alloy with titanium and nickel as the primary constituents, meeting the compositional criteria for high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled aging heat treatment (for example, holding at approximately 700°C for about 10 hours) designed to induce the formation of coherent nano-scale precipitates.
generation.conditions: The alloy must contain at least five elements at 5–35 at% each with titanium and nickel in the highest concentrations; the aging treatment should be carried out near 700°C (±50°C) for roughly 10 hours (±2 hours). Testing is to be done at elevated temperatures (e.g., around 800°C) relevant to intended applications.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a fine distribution of coherent nano-precipitates within the matrix.
generation.mechanism: The nano-precipitates hinder dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding, which are the primary deformation modes at elevated temperatures. This precipitation strengthening leads to an increase in the yield strength and creep resistance of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: The heat-treated alloy will exhibit higher yield strength and improved creep resistance at elevated temperatures relative to the as-cast alloy without the aging intervention.
generation.baseline: The elevated-temperature mechanical properties (e.g., yield strength and creep rupture life) of the as-cast, single-phase, titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy without any post-casting heat treatment.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are expected within the specified heat treatment window. Deviations from the optimal aging temperature or time may result in insufficient or excessive precipitate coarsening, which could negate the strengthening effect, particularly at temperatures above 800°C.
generation.uncertainty: Precise kinetics of nano-precipitate formation and their long-term thermal stability under prolonged elevated-temperature exposure are not fully determined, introducing uncertainty about the durability of the mechanical improvements.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of samples of the titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy. Subject one group to the controlled aging treatment (e.g., 700°C for 10 hours) and leave the other group in the as-cast condition. Perform high-temperature mechanical tests (such as compressive creep or elevated-temperature tensile tests at around 800°C) on both sets. Concurrently, use transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to characterize the presence, size, and distribution of precipitates in the aged samples.
measurements: Creep rupture life (or similar high-temperature creep resistance metric)
Microstructural features (size and distribution of nano-precipitates via TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the heat-treated samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in yield strength and creep resistance at elevated temperatures compared to the as-cast samples, or if no coherent nano-precipitates are observed, then the hypothesis is falsified.
